# IMovementService

**Interface** · namespace `VRFramework.Core.Runtime` · assembly `VRFramework.Core.Runtime` · [view source](https://git.cie-group.cz/vr-framework/vrf4/core/-/blob/main/Runtime/Scripts/Core/IMovementService.cs#L14)

What the framework expects of a movement module: getting the player from one marked standing
place to another, and being switched off while a step needs the player to stay put. Obtained
from [`RuntimeRegistry`](/api/vrframework-core-runtime/RuntimeRegistry).

Placing the player somewhere unmarked is not this - that is
[`Recenter(Component, bool)`](/api/vrframework-core-runtime/IInteractionService#recenter-component-boolean), which exists for scripted moves.

```csharp
public interface IMovementService
```

**Derived:** [`MovementModule`](/api/vrframework-movement-runtime/MovementModule)

## Properties

### CanTeleport {#canteleport}

Whether the player may teleport at all. Set false while a step needs them where they are;
any aim in progress is dropped straight away.

```csharp

```

### StandingAt {#standingat}

The standing place the player is at, or null when they are not at one. A scene reads this
to ask where the player is standing without measuring distances itself.

```csharp
Component StandingAt { get; }
```

**Returns** [`Component`](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/Component.html)

## Methods

### TeleportTo(Component) {#teleportto-component}

Moves the player to a standing place, as if they had aimed at it. Ignores
[`CanTeleport`](/api/vrframework-core-runtime/IMovementService#canteleport), since the caller is the one deciding.

```csharp
void TeleportTo(Component destination)
```
